Guides

What to know before the recipes.

Short findings first. The longer explanation is on the same page, and the sources are linked.

Foundations

What the first foods are actually for

The job of food in the second half of the first year is iron, energy, and learning to eat. It is not a target for protein percentages.

When to start

The useful window is after four months and by about six. Readiness is a set of skills, and age still has a floor.

Spoon, fingers, or both

Purées, finger foods, and a mixture of the two can all feed a baby well. The arguments about identity are louder than the evidence.

Choosing ingredients

Variety, including bitter greens, matters more than an organic label. A short list of foods is genuinely unsuitable.

Cooking and seasoning

Herbs, a mild spice, and a spoon of oil do more for a baby’s food than salt or sugar ever will.

Tools, hygiene, and the freezer

A knife, a pot, and a fridge discipline matter more than a drawer of baby gadgets.

At the table

What to introduce, and when

There is no mandatory calendar of single vegetables. There is a reason to bring allergens in early and to keep them in the diet.

Introducing allergens

Delaying peanut, egg, and milk does not prevent allergy. For most babies the safer plan is to start them, in a safe texture, and keep them coming.

Portions, texture, and milk

Appetite is a better measure than a spoon count. Milk remains the main drink until the first birthday.

A week, in outline

These are patterns, not prescriptions. Swap in whatever iron food and whatever allergen you are practising.

How the meal happens

What you serve is your decision. Whether it is eaten, and how much, is the child’s. Pressure is a poor teacher.

Gagging and choking

Gagging is loud and useful. Choking is quiet and is an emergency. Learn the hands-on response before you need it.

Health and the short list

Picky eating

Suspicion of new food is a normal toddler stage. Growth, not the day’s plate, tells you when to ask for help.

When a child is ill

Familiar food, enough fluid, and the usual milk. A sick day is a bad day to diagnose an allergy or to start a new one.

Teething

Cold food and something firm to chew are enough. Amber necklaces and benzocaine gels are not.

Vitamins and minerals

Vitamin D is a supplement decision from the first days. Iron is a food decision from six months. The rest follows the diet.
